addedLines:
- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.content:
name: Update vendorHash for dependabot Go bumps

# Dependabot bumps to go.mod/go.sum invalidate the proxyVendor FOD hash in
# default.nix, which fails the nix-build CI gate. This workflow detects the
# drift, computes the new hash via scripts/update-nix-vendorhash.sh, and
# pushes the update back to the dependabot branch so the gate goes green
# without a maintainer round-trip.
#
# Tracked under beads-bz5.
#
# Why pull_request_target (not pull_request):
#   GitHub gives the GITHUB_TOKEN read-only permissions on `pull_request`
#   workflows triggered by dependabot, regardless of declared `permissions:`.
#   `pull_request_target` runs in the trusted context of the base branch with
#   full token permissions, which is required to push back to the PR branch.
#
# Safety against pull_request_target abuse:
#   - The job only runs when github.actor is dependabot[bot] AND the PR head
#     is on the upstream repo (head.repo.full_name == github.repository).
#     Dependabot never opens PRs from forks, so this combination is not
#     reachable from an external contributor.
#   - We explicitly check out the PR head SHA to operate on dependabot's
#     bumped go.mod/go.sum. Because dependabot is the only allowed actor and
#     never modifies scripts/, the trust boundary is the dependabot bot
#     itself — this is the same trust posture the project already accepts
#     when merging dependabot PRs.
#   - No force-push. Single commit with attribution.
#
# Caveat:
#   GitHub does not retrigger pull_request workflow runs for commits
#   authored by GITHUB_TOKEN. After this workflow pushes, the existing
#   nix-build.yml check on this PR will remain stuck on the pre-fix commit.
#   Maintainers either re-run nix-build manually, or this workflow's own
#   success acts as the green signal that the hash is correct.

on:
  pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: update-vendor-hash-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  update-vendor-hash:
    name: Update default.nix vendorHash
    if: >-
      github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR head
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v6
        with:
          # pull_request_target defaults to the base ref. Explicitly check
          # out the PR head so we operate on dependabot's bumped go.mod/sum.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@d96678350ffd6a456235832eb11e1c491589b7bb # v3

      - name: Capture pre-update vendorHash
        id: pre
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OLD_HASH=$(grep 'vendorHash = ' default.nix | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
          echo "old_hash=$OLD_HASH" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Pre-update vendorHash: $OLD_HASH"

      - name: Update vendorHash
        run: ./scripts/update-nix-vendorhash.sh

version: 2
updates:
  # Go modules
  - package-ecosystem: "gomod"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    labels:
      - "dependencies"
      - "go"
    # Group minor/patch Go bumps into a single PR. Every gomod bump rewrites
    # go.sum, which invalidates the nix vendorHash in default.nix; N singleton
    # PRs mean N vendorHash bot-commits and N '@dependabot recreate' rounds
    # after each merge (see update-vendor-hash.yml caveat). One grouped PR
    # gets one bot-computed hash. Majors stay separate so a breaking bump
    # cannot block the routine group.
    groups:
      go-deps:
        applies-to: version-updates
        update-types:
          - "minor"
          - "patch"

  # GitHub Actions
  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    labels:
      - "dependencies"
      - "ci"
    groups:
      actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns:
          - "*"

  # Python (beads-mcp)
  - package-ecosystem: "uv"
    directory: "/integrations/beads-mcp"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    labels:
      - "dependencies"
      - "python"
      - "mcp"
    groups:
      beads-mcp-python:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns:
          - "*"

input.content:
## Why

Dependabot currently opens one PR per bump. For Go modules that shape is actively expensive here: every gomod bump rewrites `go.sum`, which invalidates the nix `vendorHash` in `default.nix`. The `update-vendor-hash` workflow then pushes a bot commit to each PR, after which dependabot refuses plain rebases ("edited by someone other than Dependabot") — so each merge forces `@dependabot recreate` plus a fresh CI cycle on every remaining single. Yesterday's batch (five gomod PRs: #5017, #5018, #5020, #5021, plus #4702 which has been stuck in this loop since July 10) is the live example.

## What

Add dependabot `groups` per ecosystem:

- **gomod**: minor + patch version bumps land as one grouped PR — one bot-computed vendorHash, one CI cycle. Majors stay ungrouped so a breaking bump can't hold the routine group hostage.
- **github-actions**: all version bumps grouped (low-risk pinned-action bumps like #5015/#5016/#5019).
- **uv (beads-mcp)**: all version bumps grouped (dev deps like #5022/#5023).

Schedules, PR limits, and labels are unchanged.

## Effect on the open singles

When this lands, dependabot immediately re-checks the changed ecosystems, opens grouped PRs, and closes the superseded singletons itself — no manual cleanup of #4702/#5017/#5018/#5020/#5021 needed.

Sweep complete. All 10 dependabot PRs are dispositioned, and the structural fix is in flight.

## What I found

- **Main was red**, which hard-blocks all merges: last night's Nightly Full Tests failed on `TestInitCancel_E2E` — a Feb-2026 test, green the previous 7 nights, that timed out waiting for a prompt under full-suite load. Classic flake; I reran the failed job (was still running at close).
- **The real problem is structural, not the PRs.** Every Go-module bump rewrites `go.sum`, which invalidates the nix `vendorHash`; the auto-fix workflow pushes a bot commit, after which dependabot refuses to rebase and CI never runs on the new head. That's why #4702 has been stuck since July 10 through ~60 patrol attempts, and why the four fresh gomod PRs (#5017/#5018/#5020/#5021) showed "no checks". Merging them one-by-one would mean an `@dependabot recreate` + full-CI round per merge.

## What I did

- **Opened gastownhall/beads#5038**: adds dependabot `groups` config — gomod minor/patch bumps arrive as **one grouped PR** (majors stay solo so a breaking bump can't block the group), actions and Python deps grouped wholesale. A grouped PR is dependabot-authored, so it gets a single bot-computed vendorHash, and dependabot auto-closes the five superseded gomod singles when it regroups. I rejected hand-rolling a combined PR: no nix on this machine to compute the hash, and the hash workflow only fires for dependabot.
- **Handed the five independent PRs to the patrol** (actions bumps #5015/#5016/#5019, Python dev-deps #5022/#5023 — three fully green, two with one flaky proxied-dolt shard the patrol will rerun), plus #5038 itself. Per repo policy, no in-session merging.
- **Paper trail**: disposition comment on #4702; follow-up bead mybd-ysu1 (blocked on #5038's bead) captures the post-landing steps, including the gotcha that the grouped PR needs a close/reopen to get CI onto the bot commit, and a watch item on the anthropic-sdk-go 1.45→1.61 jump; updated the `beads-nix-vendorhash-gosum` memory; report committed at `reports/2026-07-25-dependabot-pr-sweep.md`. Git and Dolt both pushed.

The session-close check warns about the six handoff beads left `in_progress` — that's the babysitter pattern working as designed (patrol owns those tails). It also flagged mybd-wo8r (a coffeegoddd PR review) as in-progress, but that's another session's work sharing the coarse session stamp — I didn't touch it.

- Group names `go-deps`, `actions`, `beads-mcp-python` are unique within their ecosystem blocks (uniqueness is only required per-ecosystem, so no collision risk even if reused). No schema fix required — this passes the only validation gate.

**2. 0.x semver bumps land in the gomod group — info (intended, but caveat the rationale).**
Dependabot classifies by raw semver position, so `testcontainers-go 0.42.0 → 0.43.0` is `version-update:semver-minor` and **will** land in `go-deps`. That is the desired outcome (fewer singletons). No config change needed, but consider softening the comment to note that 0.x breaking changes can still enter the group. Nit-level doc accuracy.

**3. Security updates stay singleton — info, optional add.**
With every group scoped `applies-to: version-updates`, security-update PRs remain ungrouped singletons. This is mostly fine here: the `update-vendor-hash` workflow keys on `github.actor == dependabot[bot]` + go.mod/go.sum paths, so it *does* auto-fix the vendorHash on a security gomod PR too — the recreate cascade only bites when multiple concurrent gomod PRs exist, which is rare for security bumps. A `go-security` group (`applies-to: security-updates`) is a reasonable low-cost add if concurrent security bumps ever appear, but it is not required and there's a real argument for keeping urgent security fixes individually reviewable/mergeable. Leave as-is; note for later.

Landing a `groups` config on `main` triggers dependabot to re-evaluate the affected ecosystems; it opens the grouped PR(s) and closes the singletons it now considers superseded (#5017/#5018/#5020/#5021). 1	## Verdict: fix-first
2	
3	The YAML is syntactically and schema-valid, but two behavioral assumptions should be fixed before merge.
4	
5	### Blocking findings
6	
7	1. **Breaking pre-1.0 Go updates will enter the routine group.**
8	
9	Dependabot mechanically classifies `x.y.z` as major/minor/patch. Therefore `0.42.0 → 0.43.0` is a **minor** update and matches [the `go-deps` rule](/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/dependabot-groups/.github/dependabot.yml:18). Both [#4702](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4702) and [#5017](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5017) qualify, despite testcontainers v0.43 explicitly containing breaking changes. This contradicts the comment that breaking bumps cannot block routine updates. [GitHub’s reference confirms the numeric classification](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference).
10	
11	Fix: isolate testcontainers ahead of the catch-all group:
12	
13	```yaml
14	groups:
15	  testcontainers:
16	    applies-to: version-updates
17	    patterns:
18	      - "github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go*"
19	
20	  go-deps:
21	    applies-to: version-updates
22	    exclude-patterns:
23	      - "github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go*"
24	    update-types:
25	      - "minor"
26	      - "patch"
27	```
28	
29	That keeps the coupled root/module updates together without mixing them into routine bumps. Also change “breaking bump” to “SemVer-major bump”; Dependabot cannot infer breaking behavior from pre-1.0 release notes.
30	
31	2. **The promised automatic migration of the five open Go PRs is not reliable.**
32	
33	As of July 25, [#4702](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4702), [#5017](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5017), [#5018](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5018), [#5020](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5020), and [#5021](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5021) are all open. That exactly saturates `open-pull-requests-limit: 5`.
34	
35	GitHub says a Dependabot configuration change triggers an update run, but also says no additional version-update PR is opened while the limit is reached. Automatic close-and-replace behavior is explicitly documented for first enabling grouped **security** updates, not version grouping. [Dependabot PR behavior](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependabot-pull-requests), [grouped security behavior](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/secure-your-dependencies/configure-security-updates).
36	
37	Fix the PR description to remove the guarantee. Use an explicit migration plan: temporarily raise the Go limit, trigger “Check for updates,” verify the grouped PR appears, close superseded singles, then restore the limit—or free a slot first and manually trigger the update.
38	
39	### Other footguns
40	
41	- `actions` and `beads-mcp-python` use `patterns: ["*"]` with no `update-types`, so they intentionally group **majors too**. Current [#5015](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5015) and [#5019](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5019) are Actions majors; [#5022](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5022) is Ruff `0.15 → 0.16`, another potentially breaking pre-1.0 minor. Either document that risk coupling explicitly or restrict/isolate risky updates.
42	- Security updates remain singleton because every rule says `applies-to: version-updates`. That is reasonable: security PRs remain urgent and are not counted against the configured five-version-PR limit.
43	- Custom labels are fine: labels on each ecosystem block apply to grouped PRs as well. Missing custom labels would be silently ignored.
44	- `uv` is not an experimental concern: Dependabot uv version updates have been GA since March 2025, and this repository is already receiving uv PRs. [GitHub’s uv GA announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-03-13-dependabot-version-updates-now-support-uv-in-general-availability/).
45	- The [vendorHash workflow](/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/.github/workflows/update-vendor-hash.yml:36) remains compatible with grouped Go PRs: the PR still touches `go.mod`/`go.sum`, is Dependabot-authored, and should produce one hash-fix commit.
46	
47	### Schema result
48	
49	No schema defect found:
50	
51	- `groups` and `applies-to: version-updates` are valid.
52	- Group-level values are correctly `minor`/`patch`, not the longer `version-update:semver-*` values used by `allow`/`ignore`.
53	- Omitting `patterns` is valid and means all dependency names pass that criterion; Dependabot’s current implementation explicitly defaults absent patterns to a match. [Dependabot core implementation](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core/blob/dc2e4422da8beef505376e1e26bc1632dfae3d57/common/lib/dependabot/dependency_group.rb).
54	- `patterns: ["*"]` is valid.
55	
56	So this will not silently disable Dependabot—but its current operational and risk-isolation claims are incorrect enough to warrant **fix-first**.

### Blocking findings

1. **Breaking pre-1.0 Go updates will enter the routine group.**

Therefore `0.42.0 → 0.43.0` is a **minor** update and matches [the `go-deps` rule](/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/dependabot-groups/.github/dependabot.yml:18).
```yaml
groups:
  testcontainers:
    applies-to: version-updates

    applies-to: version-updates

```

2. **The promised automatic migration of the five open Go PRs is not reliable.**

As of July 25, [#4702](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4702), [#5017](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5017), [#5018](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5018), [#5020](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5020), and [#5021](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/5021) are all open. input.content:
## Why

Dependabot currently opens one PR per bump. For Go modules that shape is actively expensive here: every gomod bump rewrites `go.sum`, which invalidates the nix `vendorHash` in `default.nix`. The `update-vendor-hash` workflow then pushes a bot commit to each PR, after which dependabot refuses plain rebases ("edited by someone other than Dependabot") — so each merge forces `@dependabot recreate` plus a fresh CI cycle on every remaining single. Yesterday's batch (five gomod PRs: #5017, #5018, #5020, #5021, plus #4702 which has been stuck in this loop since July 10) is the live example.

## What

Add dependabot `groups` per ecosystem:

- **gomod / `go-deps`**: minor + patch version bumps land as one grouped PR — one bot-computed vendorHash, one CI cycle. SemVer-majors stay ungrouped so they can't block the routine group. (Caveat: dependabot classifies by version arithmetic only, so pre-1.0 modules that break in "minor" bumps still ride the group — except the one we know does, below.)
- **gomod / `testcontainers`**: `testcontainers-go` and its `modules/dolt` child must bump in lockstep and routinely break in 0.x minors, so they get their own group — always coupled together, never blocking `go-deps`.
- **gomod limit 5 → 10**: the five open singles exactly saturate the old limit, and dependabot opens no new version PR while the limit is saturated — the grouped PR could be wedged out during migration.
- **github-actions**: all version bumps grouped (low-risk pinned-action bumps like #5015/#5016/#5019).
- **uv (beads-mcp)**: all version bumps grouped (dev deps like #5022/#5023).

Security updates deliberately stay singleton (`applies-to: version-updates` everywhere): urgent, individually reviewable, and not counted against the version-PR limit.

## Migration of the open singles

When this lands, dependabot re-checks the changed ecosystems. Expected outcome is grouped PRs superseding #4702/#5017/#5018/#5020/#5021, but auto-close of existing version singles is not documented as guaranteed — so the plan is: verify the grouped go PRs appear (Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot → "Check for updates" if needed), then manually close any singles dependabot leaves open. #4702 carries non-dependabot commits and is the most likely to need a manual close. Tracked in the maintainer queue (mybd-ysu1).

## Review

Independently reviewed pre-merge by two model families: claude-opus-tier reviewer (approve, doc nits) and codex gpt-5.6-sol (fix-first). Both fix-first findings — testcontainers isolation and the PR-limit saturation — are incorporated in the second commit.

## Why

This PR is the fix for red CI on `main` — it now carries **two** independent test-only fixes, both for tests that fail while the product behavior is correct.

### 1. Nightly: `TestInitCancel_E2E` deadline exhaustion

Nightly Full Tests went red overnight (run 30141630769, both attempts) on "timeout waiting for prompt" with empty output after exactly 5.02s.

- The test's 5s deadline races `bd init --contributor` startup: the embedded-dolt store is created **before** the wizard prints its first byte, so slow startup looks like "no prompt, no output".
- Nightly timings show margin exhaustion, not a flake or regression: **4.71s** (07-23, pass) → **4.92s** (07-24, pass) → **5.02s** (07-25, killed). The rerun failed identically; in isolation with the same flags the test passes in ~1.2s.
- Fix: widen the deadline to 60s. It guards against a *hung* init, not startup speed; 60s still fails fast against the suite's 30-minute timeout.

### 2. Contract corpus: `TestProtocol_GrantingReplicaRoundTripsJSONL` false positive

This PR's first CI run surfaced a second red: the new wy-jpd3.7 replica-guard test fails deterministically on its first Contract corpus outing — with the guard visibly *working* (`"count": 0`, `"reclaimed": null`, status kept).

- The test asserts non-reclamation via `strings.Contains(reclaimOut, leased)`, but `tryRunEnv` captures **CombinedOutput**, and `warnReplica`'s stderr audit line ("reclaim: skipping `<id>` …") names the very id being asserted absent.
- Fix: parse the reclaimed ids out of the JSON payload (stdout is the machine truth — `warnReplica` deliberately keeps audit lines off stdout) and use the same helper for the `--any-replica` positive assertion, which was passing only incidentally.
- Fails before / passes after: `go test -tags gms_pure_go -run TestProtocol_GrantingReplicaRoundTripsJSONL ./cmd/bd/protocol`

## Validation

Both tests pass locally with their CI flags. Note per-PR CI does not exercise the integration-tagged init test; the authoritative re-check for that half is a `workflow_dispatch` nightly (`full-test`) after merge, which I'll trigger. The Contract corpus job on this PR exercises the second fix directly.

# Dependabot PR sweep — 2026-07-25

Sweep bead: mybd-i0pd. Scope: all 10 open dependabot PRs on gastownhall/beads
(#5015–#5023 opened 2026-07-24, plus #4702 stuck since 2026-07-10).

## Findings

- **Main was red**, blocking every merge via preflight: Nightly Full Tests
  failed at `4951412f` on `TestInitCancel_E2E` ("timeout waiting for prompt",
  5s kill under full-suite load). The test dates from 2026-02-10 and the
  nightly was green the previous 7 nights — load-induced flake, not the
  HasPersistedRemote commit. Reran the failed job (run 30141630769).
- **The gomod singleton shape is structurally broken here.** Every gomod bump
  rewrites `go.sum` → invalidates nix `vendorHash` → `update-vendor-hash.yml`
  pushes a bot commit → dependabot then refuses plain rebases → each merge
  forces `@dependabot recreate` + full CI on all remaining singles. GITHUB_TOKEN
  bot pushes also don't retrigger CI, so heads show "no checks" (#5017/#5018/
  #5020/#5021 were all in this state). #4702 burned two weeks and a day of
  patrol cycles this way (see mybd-9rgr notes), ending merge-blocked after a
  manual conflict-resolution merge skipped the vendorHash workflow (that
  incident is also mybd-cof8's subject).
- A locally-built combined PR was considered and rejected: no nix on this
  machine to compute vendorHash, and the workflow only fires for
  dependabot-authored PRs.

## Dispositions

| PR | What | Action |
|----|------|--------|
| #5015 setup-go 7.0.0 | actions bump | pr-handoff → mybd-21t0 (1 shard flaky-red: TestProxiedServerConfigSetMany; patrol reruns) |
| #5016 checkout 7.0.1 | actions bump | pr-handoff → mybd-kiaz (same flaky shard) |
| #5019 setup-python 7.0.0 | actions bump | green; pr-handoff → mybd-ihj9 |
| #5022 ruff 0.16.0 | uv dev dep | green; pr-handoff → mybd-340o |
| #5023 types-requests | uv dev dep | green; pr-handoff → mybd-haks |
| #5017 testcontainers-go 0.43 | gomod | superseded by grouping (below) |
| #5018 goldmark 1.8.4 | gomod | superseded by grouping |
| #5020 go-sqlmock 1.5.2 | gomod | superseded by grouping |
| #5021 anthropic-sdk-go 1.61 | gomod | superseded by grouping |
| #4702 testcontainers dolt 0.43 | gomod, stuck | superseded by grouping; disposition comment posted; mybd-9rgr blocked on mybd-8usj |

## The fix: dependabot `groups` (PR #5038)

gastownhall/beads#5038 (branch `maphew:chore/dependabot-groups`) adds `groups`
to `.github/dependabot.yml`: gomod minor+patch as one grouped PR (majors stay
solo so a breaking bump can't block the group), actions grouped wholesale, uv
grouped wholesale. One grouped gomod PR = one bot-computed vendorHash = one CI
cycle, and dependabot auto-closes the superseded singles when it regroups
(config changes trigger an immediate dependabot run). Handed off → mybd-8usj.

content.content: Any change to beads go.sum invalidates the nix proxyVendor FOD hash in default.nix. The update-vendor-hash.yml workflow auto-fixes this ONLY for dependabot-authored PRs (pull_request_target gated on actor==dependabot[bot]); maintainer PRs that touch go.sum must run scripts/update-nix-vendorhash.sh (needs nix) or merging will break the nix-build workflow on main. Learned 2026-07-24: PR gastownhall/beads#4942 x/text bump merged without it and turned main's nix-build red; repaired by merging recreated dependabot PR #4701 whose bot-computed vendorHash covered the new go.sum. Also: the bot's vendorHash commit makes dependabot refuse rebase ('edited by someone other than Dependabot') — use '@dependabot recreate', and note recreated-PR CI attaches to the pre-fix commit, so nix job failures there are expected; the Update-vendorHash job's success is the green signal. UPDATE 2026-07-25: gastownhall/beads#5038 adds dependabot groups config (gomod minor/patch as ONE grouped PR, actions and uv grouped) so this cascade class disappears — one grouped PR gets one bot-computed vendorHash. Do NOT recreate/babysit singleton gomod dependabot PRs; they auto-close when dependabot regroups after 5038 lands. Grouped-PR gotcha remains: bot vendorHash commit does not retrigger CI on head (GITHUB_TOKEN) — close/reopen the PR to start CI on the head SHA before pr-handoff. See mybd-ysu1. # Dependabot PR sweep — 2026-07-25

Sweep bead: mybd-i0pd. Scope: all 10 open dependabot PRs on gastownhall/beads
(#5015–#5023 opened 2026-07-24, plus #4702 stuck since 2026-07-10).

## Findings

- **Main was red**, blocking every merge via preflight: Nightly Full Tests
  failed at `4951412f` on `TestInitCancel_E2E` ("timeout waiting for prompt",
  5s kill under full-suite load). The test dates from 2026-02-10 and the
  nightly was green the previous 7 nights — load-induced flake, not the
  HasPersistedRemote commit. Reran the failed job (run 30141630769).
- **The gomod singleton shape is structurally broken here.** Every gomod bump
  rewrites `go.sum` → invalidates nix `vendorHash` → `update-vendor-hash.yml`
  pushes a bot commit → dependabot then refuses plain rebases → each merge
  forces `@dependabot recreate` + full CI on all remaining singles. GITHUB_TOKEN
  bot pushes also don't retrigger CI, so heads show "no checks" (#5017/#5018/
  #5020/#5021 were all in this state). #4702 burned two weeks and a day of
  patrol cycles this way (see mybd-9rgr notes), ending merge-blocked after a
  manual conflict-resolution merge skipped the vendorHash workflow (that
  incident is also mybd-cof8's subject).
- A locally-built combined PR was considered and rejected: no nix on this
  machine to compute vendorHash, and the workflow only fires for
  dependabot-authored PRs.

## Dispositions

| PR | What | Action |
|----|------|--------|
| #5015 setup-go 7.0.0 | actions bump | pr-handoff → mybd-21t0 (1 shard flaky-red: TestProxiedServerConfigSetMany; patrol reruns) |
| #5016 checkout 7.0.1 | actions bump | pr-handoff → mybd-kiaz (same flaky shard) |
| #5019 setup-python 7.0.0 | actions bump | green; pr-handoff → mybd-ihj9 |
| #5022 ruff 0.16.0 | uv dev dep | green; pr-handoff → mybd-340o |
| #5023 types-requests | uv dev dep | green; pr-handoff → mybd-haks |
| #5017 testcontainers-go 0.43 | gomod | superseded by grouping (below) |
| #5018 goldmark 1.8.4 | gomod | superseded by grouping |
| #5020 go-sqlmock 1.5.2 | gomod | superseded by grouping |
| #5021 anthropic-sdk-go 1.61 | gomod | superseded by grouping |
| #4702 testcontainers dolt 0.43 | gomod, stuck | superseded by grouping; disposition comment posted; mybd-9rgr blocked on mybd-8usj |

## The fix: dependabot `groups` (PR #5038)

gastownhall/beads#5038 (branch `maphew:chore/dependabot-groups`) adds `groups`
to `.github/dependabot.yml`: gomod minor+patch as one grouped PR (majors stay
solo so a breaking bump can't block the group), actions grouped wholesale, uv
grouped wholesale. One grouped gomod PR = one bot-computed vendorHash = one CI
cycle, and dependabot auto-closes the superseded singles when it regroups
(config changes trigger an immediate dependabot run). Handed off → mybd-8usj.

## Tails (all with patrol / future agents, not this session)

- mybd-8usj — #5038 merge (patrol; waits for base green).
- mybd-ysu1 (blocked on mybd-8usj) — after regrouping: close/reopen the grouped
  gomod PR to get CI onto the bot-commit head SHA, hand off to patrol, watch
  the anthropic-sdk-go 1.45→1.61 jump (used in `cmd/bd/find_duplicates.go`,
  `internal/compact/haiku.go`), then close mybd-9rgr + itself.
- Five singleton handoff beads above.

Nightly rerun and #5038 CI were in progress at session close.

## Addendum: bring-home session (same day)

Owner asked for an independent review of #5038 and to see the sweep through.

**Dual review of #5038** (claude reviewer: approve-as-is; codex gpt-5.6-sol:
fix-first). Codex caught two real gaps, both incorporated (commit 2a732e082):

- testcontainers-go + modules/dolt must bump in lockstep and break in 0.x
  "minors", so they got their own `testcontainers` group, excluded from
  `go-deps` — coupled together, never blocking routine bumps.
- The five open gomod singles exactly saturated `open-pull-requests-limit: 5`,
  and dependabot opens no new version PR at the limit — the grouped PR could
  be wedged out. Raised to 10. PR body's auto-supersession promise softened to
  a verified migration plan (mybd-ysu1).

**The nightly "flake" wasn't one.** The rerun failed identically: the 5s
prompt deadline in `TestInitCancel_E2E` races embedded-dolt store creation,
which crept 4.71s → 4.92s → 5.02s across three nightlies. Margin exhaustion.
Fix: 60s hang-guard deadline.

**#5039's own CI then exposed a second latent red**: the wy-jpd3.7 replica-guard
test `TestProtocol_GrantingReplicaRoundTripsJSONL` asserts non-reclamation via
`strings.Contains` on *combined* output, but `warnReplica`'s stderr audit line
echoes the issue id — a correctly-declined reclaim fails the test
deterministically, on every PR's Contract corpus job from its first outing.
Fix: parse reclaimed ids from the JSON payload (stdout is the machine truth);
fails-before/passes-after verified locally.

Both fixes travel as gastownhall/beads#5039 (`test: fix red main`), the
policy-sanctioned only-mergeable PR while main is red. Chain: #5039 green →
in-session merge → workflow_dispatch nightly full-test → base green → patrol
merges #5038 + remaining singles (#5016, #5023 already landed mid-session) →
dependabot regroups. Bead chain: mybd-kney → mybd-8usj → mybd-ysu1.
